definitions.explanation: A rank of nobility, third in the five-rank peerage system. Equivalent to 'count' in continental European nobility or 'earl' in British peerage. Also used in the former Japanese peerage system (kazoku) established in 1884.

examples.japanese: {伯爵|はくしゃく}の{称号|しょうごう}を{与|あた}えられた。
examples.english: He was given the title of count.

examples.japanese: ドラキュラ{伯爵|はくしゃく}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{吸血鬼|きゅうけつき}のキャラクターだ。
examples.english: Count Dracula is a famous vampire character.

examples.japanese: {明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}に{華族|かぞく}{制度|せいど}が{設|もう}けられ、{公爵|こうしゃく}・{侯爵|こうしゃく}・{伯爵|はくしゃく}・{子爵|ししゃく}・{男爵|だんしゃく}の{五|いつ}つの{爵位|しゃくい}が{定|さだ}められた。
examples.english: In the Meiji era, a peerage system was established with five ranks: duke, marquis, count, viscount, and baron.

notes:
One of the five ranks in the Japanese {華族|かぞく} peerage system (1884-1947), modeled after European nobility.

THE FIVE RANKS:
・{公爵|こうしゃく} (duke/prince)
・{侯爵|こうしゃく} (marquis)
・{伯爵|はくしゃく} (count/earl)
・{子爵|ししゃく} (viscount)
・{男爵|だんしゃく} (baron)

USAGE NOTES:
Most commonly encountered in translations of European literature and history (e.g., {伯爵|はくしゃく}モンテ・クリスト — The Count of Monte Cristo) or discussions of Meiji-era Japanese history. The female form is {伯爵|はくしゃく}{夫人|ふじん} (countess).
